composition.serve_who: GMMS 108’-110a is the vessel’s 24 V DC service-supply one-line. It principally serves the DC distribution system by showing how four MAPS outputs, one 230 V AC/24 V DC standby converter, and the auxiliary-service battery are selected onto the +24 V service bus, then distributed to the forward/aft DC panels, main bilge pump, fire pump, and low-voltage BAE panel. The left side also shows the port/starboard HVPDU 600 V buses feeding the MAPS units; the lower and centre regions show shared return, sensing, selector, terminal-strip, relay, and PC-card infrastructure. Named outgoing loads are attached to their own equipment nodes rather than absorbed into the panel.

infrastructure.system_name: HV Power Distribution Unit — port and starboard HVPDU
facts: The PORT and STBD 600 V DC bus bars are the two HVPDU high-voltage buses; they are not a separate backbone system.
Each HVPDU bank shows Q1-Q4 rated 32 A; only the Q4-to-MAPS connection is drawn on this sheet, so no destinations are assigned to Q1-Q3 here.
Each side has two 500 A main fuses F1/F2 in the HVPDU bus structure before the lower/upper bus sections.
PORT Q4 supplies PORT MAPS-1/2; STBD Q4 supplies STBD MAPS-1/2.
The HVPDU and DC service distribution remain distinct systems despite both participating in the conversion chain.
Owns the +24 V SERVICE BUS, NEGATIVE BUS, SHUNT #1 500 A/50 mV, source isolator bank SW1-SW5/SO1-SO5, terminal strips, relay bank Re1/Re2, and BAE/AUX selector/PC-card interface.

Five selectable positive source paths reach the common shunt/service bus: PORT MAPS channels through F1/F2 and CT1/CT2; STBD MAPS channels through F3/F4 and CT3/CT4; and the standby 230 V AC/24 V DC converter through F18 125 A and CT5.
The standby source path is drawn as 230 V AC L/N → 24 V DC converter rated 110 A → F18 125 A → CT5 → SW5/SO5 → SHUNT #1 → +24 V SERVICE BUS; its AC source identity is off-sheet.
The +24 V SERVICE BUS owns the FWD DC PANEL feeder F5 100 A via SW6 and the AFT DC PANEL feeder F6 200 A via SW7.

All named returns for FWD DC PANEL, AFT DC PANEL, BILGE PUMP, FIRE PUMP, GEN START BAT., EMERGENCY BAT. and AUX SERVICE BAT. terminate on the common NEGATIVE BUS, which is bonded to ship’s ground as drawn.

The source-isolator command/indication network uses T/S S terminals 4-7 and 8-12 with relays Re1/Re2; several external command conductors continue off-sheet, so only the locally drawn terminal-to-relay/isolator relationships are retained.
The PC CARD provides ten left and ten right interface pins, indicator channels, BAE/AUX selection, NEG and +EM interfaces; no load identity is assigned to unlabeled indicator channels.
CTB1-CTB6 are noted as QI-POWER-485-300-LV and CTB7 as the same type for EMERGENCY BAT.; this is panel instrumentation type data, not seven separate systems.

discarded_as_clutter: Drawing title/revision/date/customer and company title-block data
Repeated acronym definitions for HVPDU and MAPS after applying them to the identified systems
Repeated CTB1-CTB7 legend rows after retaining the common type and CTB7 emergency-battery note in infrastructure
Diamond “70” wire-size callouts treated as conductor annotations, not devices
Duplicate terminal-strip and isolator entries from overlapping extraction regions
Unlabelled PC-card lamp-channel repeats retained only as panel infrastructure, not equipment functions
Cross-reference labels DWG 401a, 413, 110b, 113 and 114 retained only where they mark a genuine off-sheet continuation
Prior extraction’s incorrect “230V AC” rating on the NEGATIVE BUS; contextual reading is 230 V AC ground (= ship’s ground), while the bus itself is the 24 V DC negative return
uncertainties: The 230 V AC source feeding the 24 V/110 A standby converter is off-sheet and not named, so it cannot be attached to a specific AC panel from this drawing alone.

The exact command logic and normal contact positions for source isolators SO1-SO5 and relays Re1/Re2 are not fully stated; external conductors at T/S S terminals 4-12 continue off-sheet. The composition therefore states only open/closed source-path effects and does not invent an interlock.
The exact junction relationship of the ground/return branch adjacent to T/S S terminals 11 and 12 is not unambiguous at this image scale.
The downstream identity of the “LV. BAE PANEL” beyond DWG 110b is not more specific on this sheet.
CT1-CT6 measurement ratios/ranges are not printed.
The control source for SO6, SO7, SO8 and SO9 is not shown end-to-end on this sheet; their power-contact effect is clear, but their remote/local activation logic is off-sheet.
The fuse rating built into T/S E terminal 8 is not printed; only upstream QE7 is clearly rated 6 A.
